item.title: Orthogonal group sections via light bulb systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.27126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any oriented, smooth $4$--manifold $X$ diffeomorphic to $(S^2\times S^2)^{\# n}\# D^4$, this paper shows that the natural group homomorphism $$\mathrm{Mod}(X,\partial X)\to \mathrm{O}(H_2(X;\mathbb{Z}))$$ admits a section. In fact, every light bulb system in $X$ gives rise to a section, which can be characterized uniquely in terms of implanted barbell twists and implanted crossbell involutions. Moreover, all sections arising from different light bulb systems become identical after a single $S^2\times S^2$--stabilization of $X$.
item.dc:creator: Yi Liu

item.title: Weak reducibility for bridge trisections
item.description: arXiv:2610.27382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A bridge splitting of a knot is weakly reducible if it has a pair of disjoint shadows, one from above and one from below, in the splitting surface. The process of weak reduction exchanges local minima and maxima in the splitting, untelescoping the splitting and giving a method for detecting essential surfaces in the knot complement. Bridge trisections generalize bridge splittings to the setting of surfaces in 4-manifolds. We define weak reducibility in this context, giving diagrammatic conditions for carrying out a weak reduction operation on bridge splittings. We produce a partial classification of 4-bridge trisections of surfaces in $S^4$.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Lewis-Monkman

item.title: U torsion structure in Heegaard Floer homology
item.description: arXiv:2610.27646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct infinite families of Brieskorn spheres with three singular fibers for which the difference between the largest and the second largest length of U-torsion in their Heegaard Floer homology $HF^-$ increases to infinity as the family parameter increases. In particular, these families give a negative answer to the strong geography restriction on rational homology spheres. As an application, these families give the examples of integer homology spheres that are neither surgery on a knot nor large surgery on links.
item.dc:creator: Yuhui Chen, Shunyu Wan

item.title: Geometric chains of orbifolds with corners and singular homology
item.description: arXiv:2610.28446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a geometric homology theory (GHT for short). Its chains are generated by smooth maps from compact oriented orbifolds with corners to a smooth space, and two kinds of chains are set to zero: those admitting an orientation reversing automorphism, and degenerate ones, which, together with their boundaries, factor through smooth maps to orbifolds of lower dimension. Bisecting the source of a geometric chain along a hypersurface transverse to its corners changes the chain only by the boundary of an explicit prism and by prisms over its faces; cutting a geometric cycle along a regular level set of a smooth function on the target does not change its homology class. Geometric chains also behave well under products and pullbacks along fibre bundles, which overcomes some of the combinatorial rigidity of singular chains. We prove that geometric homology is naturally isomorphic to singular homology with rational coefficients for every smooth space admitting a good cover, such as smooth manifolds, orbifolds and locally finite polyhedra, and also for orbifolds with corners. The proof uses cutting operators along level sets of functions on the target, realized by explicit prisms, instead of triangulations. For continuous maps into arbitrary spaces we conjecture the same statement, and prove it for Euclidean neighbourhood retracts in degrees at most one, with surjectivity in degree two. Without the relation killing degenerate chains the comparison fails for orbifold chains: the weighted projective plane $\mathbb{P}(1,1,p)$, $p\ge5$ prime, mapped to a point is a cycle that does not bound. Applications on Morse theory and the BV structure on geometric chains of moduli spaces of bordered Riemann surfaces, following Costello and Harrelson--Voronov--Z\'u\~niga, are given.
item.dc:creator: Hao Yu

item.title: Disc-presheaves and normal invariants
item.description: arXiv:2610.26895v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this note, we elaborate on a result of Krannich--Kupers--Mehzer on Disc-presheaves. We show that equivalences of $2$-truncated Disc-presheaves of manifolds yields homotopy equivalences with trivial normal invariant. As an application, we show that two closed, simply connected manifolds are homeomorphic if and only if their $2$-truncated Disc-presheaves are equivalent.
item.dc:creator: Oliver H. Wang

item.title: Flux Vacua, Asymptotic Periods, and Relatively Anosov Representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.27077v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a topological method to detect classical flux vacua of M-theory on Calabi-Yau fourfolds with a single complex structure modulus using only asymptotic period data and monodromy information. To this end, we express the index of the F-term of the flux superpotential as a winding number along the boundary of the universal cover of the complex structure moduli space. The index evaluates to a sum over zeros and poles of a suitably normalized boundary F-term, where local contributions can be computed algebraically on a dense set of boundary points. Assuming a conjectured bound on the remaining contributions, sufficiently many sign changes of the boundary F-term guarantee a flux vacuum in the interior. We illustrate the method on the mirror Fermat sextic with explicit examples and a systematic flux scan. A main technical ingredient in our construction is a continuity result for projective period maps: we prove that the non-holomorphic (3,1)-period map extends continuously to the boundary of the covering space if the monodromy representation is relatively Anosov. In general, this property does not hold for holomorphic (4,0)-periods.
item.dc:creator: Paul Balavoine, Severin L\"ust

item.title: Tree Lattices and the Neumann-Zagier conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.27095v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A tree with integer weights on its vertices presents an integral lattice called a tree lattice. We prove that if a tree lattice is positive definite, then one of the vertex elements is irreducible, i.e. determines a facet of its Voronoi polyhedron. As a corollary, we settle a 1985 conjecture of Neumann and Zagier: if a tree lattice is isometric to the lattice of integer points in Euclidean space, then the tree contains a vertex of weight one.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Evan Greene, Ahmad Issa, Duncan McCoy

item.title: Maximal ranks of free abelian subgroups of generalized cactus groups associated with finite Coxeter systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.27716v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the maximum ranks of free abelian subgroups of generalized cactus groups associated with finite Coxeter systems. To obtain the upper bounds, we use the cubical flat torus theorem of Wise and Woodhouse. We then verify the sharpness of these upper bounds by constructing free abelian subgroups of the corresponding ranks. Our result shows that the maximal ranks of free abelian subgroups of ordinary cactus groups can be larger than conjectured by Genevois. As an application, we show that these groups are not quasi-isometric to any right-angled Artin group unless they are virtually free abelian.
item.dc:creator: Jan Kim, Junseok Kim

item.title: Classification of finite subgroups of generalized cactus groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.27721v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify the finite groups that embed into generalized cactus groups $C_W$ associated with arbitrary Coxeter systems $(W,S)$. Every finite subgroup is conjugate to a subgroup of $C_{W_T}$ for some spherical subset $T\subseteq S$. This reduces the classification to explicit lists of finite groups for the finite irreducible Coxeter systems. For types $B$, $D$, $E$, $F$, and $H$, we analyze cube stabilizers to obtain these lists. For type $I_2(p)$, we determine $C_{W(I_2(p))}$ directly from its defining presentation. We explicitly realize every listed group as a subgroup of the corresponding generalized cactus group. When $S$ is finite, we determine the largest order and all possible orders of finite subgroups of $C_W$. In type $A$, we prove directly that a finite group embeds into the ordinary cactus group $J_n$ if and only if it embeds into a Sylow $2$-subgroup of the symmetric group $S_n$. We also give weighted embedding criteria in types $A$ and $B$ and counterexamples to Genevois's conjecture on finite subgroups of cactus groups.
item.dc:creator: Junseok Kim

item.title: Median spaces with the strict separation property and superrigidity of actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.27866v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce strictly separated median spaces, prove structural results and establish superrigidity for actions of higher rank lattices on the latter. We consider two different approach, the first one relies on the construction of a boundary map and the second one is self-contained and relies on the median geometry of the space of sections taking values in a median space.
item.dc:creator: Indira Chatterji, Lamine Messaci

item.title: Towards differential expansion for generic representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.28531v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We report the first results of phenomenological analysis, based on extended set of explicitly calculated colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials in \cite{knotebook}. They concern differential expansion (DE), which separates the dependencies on the knot ${\cal K}$ and the representation $R$. %of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials. DE is well understood for symmetric and rectangular representations, while for non-rectangular $R$ even the knot-independent basis $Z_R^X$ of DE is not known. We concentrate on two issues: the possible derivation of DE and on improved characteristic of its defect. We discuss how evolution families -- twist knots, double braids and 3-pretzels -- can be used to find DE by a peculiar triangular transformation of evolution coefficients. Once $Z^R_X$ are found for particular family, they are expected to stay basically the same for arbitrary knots -- modulo controllable reductions, characterized by the defect of DE, which puts knots into different universality classes. Contrary to original expectation, these classes appear labeled not by a single number $\delta^{\cal K}$, but by a whole non-decreasing sequence $\{k_j\}$, which is squeezed between two staircases, ${\rm entier}\left(\frac{j-1}{\delta+1}\right)\leq k_j\leq{\rm entier}\left(\frac{j-1}{{\rm deg}\,\Delta}\right)$, where the upper bound involves Alexander polynomial $\Delta(q^2)$ and follows from the continuation of the Melvin--Morton--Rozansky-Kashaev limit to $A=q^{-m}$ with $m>0$, when the limit gives a {\it positive} power of Alexander. The old assumption $\delta+1={\rm deg}\,\Delta$ is oversimplified and fails for 19 non-alternating knots with 11 and 12 crossings. Last, we list the differences of non-rectangularly colored HOMFLY for various mutant pairs to demonstrate their universality (knot-independence) and nice consistency with the spirit of DE.
item.dc:creator: Ya. Kononov, A. Morozov

item.title: Hurwitz existence problem and fiber products
item.description: arXiv:2408.10874v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: With each holomorphic map $f:R\to\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$, where $R$ is a compact Riemann surface, one can associate a combinatorial datum consisting of the genus $g$ of $R$, the degree $n$ of $f$, the number $r$ of critical values of $f$, and the $r$ partitions of $n$ given by the local degrees of $f$ over these critical values. These quantities are related by the Riemann-Hurwitz formula, and the Hurwitz existence problem asks whether a combinatorial datum that fits this formula actually corresponds to some map $f$. In this paper, we use fiber products of holomorphic maps between compact Riemann surfaces to establish general criteria for the non-realizability of branch data. We also deduce from our results the theorem of Halphen, proven in 1880, concerning polynomial solutions of the equation $A(z)^a+B(z)^b=C(z)^c$, where $a,b,c$ are integers greater than one.
item.dc:creator: Fedor Pakovich

item.title: On Isolated Geometric Triangulations
item.description: arXiv:2509.01627v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Work of Kalelkar, Schleimer, and Segerman shows that, with some exceptions, the set of essential ideal triangulations of an orientable cusped hyperbolic 3-manifold is connected via 2-3 and 3-2 moves. It is natural to ask if the subgraph consisting of only those triangulations that are geometric is connected. Hoffman gives the first two examples of geometric triangulations with the property that no 2-3 or 3-2 move results in a geometric triangulation. In this paper, we introduce these as isolated geometric triangulations and show that this is not a property of small manifolds by exhibiting an infinite family of once-punctured torus bundles whose monodromy ideal triangulation is isolated.
item.dc:creator: Ian Benway

item.title: Satellites and invariants of links
item.description: arXiv:2609.33309v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An invariant $v$ of $m$-component links is called "cableable" if there exists a $k$ such that whenever a link $L'$ is obtained from a link $L=(K_1,\dots,K_m)$ by replacing each knot $K_i$ with its $(p_i,q_i)$-cable for some $p_i$ and $q_i$, we have $v(L')=(p_1\cdots p_m)^kv(L)$. The following problem is implicit in a number of papers by P. M. Akhmetiev and originates from the Arnold-Moffatt program for finding topological lower bounds for the energy of a magnetic field: Does there exist a cableable finite type invariant of links in $S^3$ which is not a function of the pairwise linking numbers? According to Akhmetiev, he solved this problem himself, with the desired invariant being defined for $3$-component links as an analytic expression involving a magnetic field modeled on the given link. We offer a different solution, with the desired invariant for $m$-component links, $m\ge 3$, being a function of the coefficients of the Conway polynomial of the link and its sublinks; the function is given explicitly when $m=3$. Moreover, we show that the cables can be replaced by arbitrary satellites. Much of the proof is a study of low degree coefficients of the Conway potential function $\Omega_L(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ expanded as a formal power series in Conway's variables $z_i=x_i-x_i^{-1}$. We also discuss type $n$ invariants which are "cableable up to an invariant of type $n-1$", some cableable invariants which are not of finite type (particularly a certain modification of Milnor's $\bar\mu$-invariants), and applications to links of solenoids.
item.dc:creator: Sergey A. Melikhov

item.title: On infinite knot families with the same HOMFLYPT polynomial
item.description: arXiv:2610.16017v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we focus on the examples constructed by Kanenobu and provide new family knots with the same HOMFLYPT polynomial invariants, which are distinguished by the Kauffman polynomial.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Matsushima

item.title: Non-geometric ideal triangulations with all edge valences at least six
item.description: arXiv:2610.25217v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Costantino, Frigerio, Martelli and Petronio conjectured that an ideal triangulation in which every edge has valence at least six can be realized by hyperbolic partially truncated tetrahedra on the compact 3-manifold it defines. We show that this is false. Starting from the figure-eight knot complement, we construct an ideal triangulation with $2688$ tetrahedra and edge valences six and eighteen whose manifold is hyperbolic with totally geodesic boundary, but which admits no such realization. The obstruction is a critical point of the covolume energy of Luo and Yang at which three tetrahedra have collapsed: convexity then excludes every geometric competitor, an Euler characteristic count excludes edges of length zero, and the critical point itself is located by a finite certificate in exact integer arithmetic. The obstruction persists in every finite cover, while a complementary theorem shows that no counterexample can have only two edge lengths or only two orbits of edges.
item.dc:creator: Ke Feng, Aijin Lin

item.title: Non-planar contact structures with Calabi-Yau Fillings and topological quantum computation
item.description: arXiv:2610.25878v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is a non-planar counterpart of the author's earlier work on planar contact structures and topological quantum computation. On a planar page every branch point is paired by a liftable arc, and the pairing matches the Ising representation exactly, in that fixing the channels of the pairs already fixes the state. Here the page has genus g and connected binding, presented as a simple degree-three cover of the disk. Every maximal system of disjoint liftable arcs then has exactly g members and leaves two branch points unused, and the half-twist interchanging the two points is not liftable, although its cube is and lifts to the identity. Ising fusion does not see that leftover pair, determining its channel from the other g and acting there only by scalars, whereas Fibonacci fusion can leave the channel undetermined. The powers of the cube then act by ten distinct relative phases on a single joint eigenspace, while the Calabi-Yau Stein filling stays fixed. An integral residue criterion supplies the Calabi-Yau test, a factorization localized on a contact connected sum is automatically Calabi-Yau, and, unlike in the planar case, a Calabi-Yau factorization need not be the shortest.
item.dc:creator: Atsuhide Mori

item.title: Geometries for Groups
item.description: arXiv:2511.03887v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a "continuous converse" to the Milnor-Schwarz lemma. Given any topological group $G$ and any left-invariant, large scale geodesic pseudometric $d$ giving an identity neighborhood finite diameter (for example, the word metric with respect to an open generating set), we construct a geodesic metric space $X$ equipped with a continuous, isometric, cobounded action of $G$ such that $(G,d)$ and $X$ are quasi-isometric via any orbit map.
item.dc:creator: Robert Alonzo Lyman
